title: Capital One Gesture Interface Patent
subtitle: A self-directed prototype effort that turned a stalled taxonomy debate into a patented gesture-based mobile banking interaction.
summary: When a large team pushed a simplistic taxonomy over user intuitiveness, Van formed a cross-functional shadow team to prototype a better path: a gesture-based interface that simplified complex banking data into human-centered insights.

sections.heading: The Conflict
body: A large team was pushing for a taxonomy and navigation flow that prioritized simplistic, random categories over user intuitiveness.

The risk was not just a messy information architecture. It was a mobile banking experience that would force customers to learn the bank's internal logic instead of helping them understand their own financial lives.

sections.heading: The Strategic Action
body: Rather than staying in sideline critique, Van formed a self-directed, cross-functional shadow team to build a working prototype of a gesture-based interface.
The prototype reframed the conversation around what customers could intuitively do, feel, and understand in context, instead of which static category label the business preferred.
bullets: Framed the concept around user value instead of technical novelty.
Created prototypes and storyboards to make the interaction feel concrete.
Prepared the narrative for both strategic review and legal evaluation.

sections.heading: Impact Beyond the Patent
body: The gesture interface, later published as US20220261083A1, reshaped how the bank approached mobile interaction. But the deeper win was organizational: the work proved that design could intervene early, make the problem tangible, and prevent business-crushing mediocrity before it hardened into product direction.
The effort also simplified complex data into human-centered insights, contributing to a customer win that helped drive a 30-day deposit increase of $10M.
bullets: Customer win: Simplified complex data into human-centered insights, leading to a 30-day deposit increase of $10M.
Organizational win: Established a Guide/Solve model where design intervened early to prevent business-crushing mediocrity.
Technical win: The gesture interface, US20220261083A1, reshaped how the bank approached mobile interaction.
